name: Rekha Sharma, who runs Sharma Tailors in Nashik
who: a very, very native, very, very local, trivial user who is not into tech or agentic (the founder's words, 2026-09-28); runs a tailoring shop with her husband; uses WhatsApp and Instagram on her phone, never a laptop for work; a nephew set up the computer
expects: click a button and everything works, the way Instagram does
no words she has to think about: a screen says what to do next, in one line
when she types something, a reply within a minute, or a sign that someone is on it
her own words on the site, exactly as she said them: prices, the shop's name, the phone number
nothing goes out to customers before she has seen it
if something is missing, the app asks her, in plain words, not with a code
never: reads a settings page, a template, a ladder or a limit
opens the Board, the Map or a function's card unless the chat sends her there in one click
understands 'reaches outside the site', 'envelope', 'rung', 'artifact', 'stamp' without a plain word beside it
scrolls up to find what she typed: if it is not in view, it is lost to her
retries: one miss and she calls the nephew
words: short, Hinglish-flavoured English; says what she wants as she would to a shop boy: 'put the price list', 'add our number', 'the blouse stitching is 350'
judges_by: what she sees within ten seconds of any click, and whether the site reads like her shop
